claims.claim: Y-style preference supervision and N-style next-item supervision learn different recommendation semantics.
evidence: Y-K0 improves binary AUC/F1 over the zero-shot base on MovieLens-1M.
N-K0 strongly outperforms Y-K0 on candidate-label ranking under Canonical Random-k5 and PopMatch-k5.
Y-K0's P(Yes)-based ranking weakens under PopMatch-k5 despite strong binary metrics.
claims.scope: MovieLens-1M; completed Y/N/M runs; ranking claims require candidate protocol labels.
limitations: Y ranking uses P(Yes)-based preference scoring, not N-task candidate-label scoring.
The result should not be phrased as a universal superiority of one supervision type.
claims.allowed_language: Y and N supervision expose a task-interface mismatch: binary preference quality does not automatically transfer to hard candidate ranking.
claims.forbidden_language: Y-K0 is a better recommender than N-K0.

claims.claim: Dedicated N supervision is the strongest LLM ranking setting, while M1 is the best unified Y/N tradeoff.
evidence: N-K0 exceeds M1 on PopMatch-k5 HR@1 by 0.0202643172 in seed 42.
N-K0 exceeds M1 on PopMatch-k5 HR@1 in seeds 42/43/44; minimum margin 0.0103964758.
M1 keeps Y-side binary performance near Y-K0 while ranking close to N-K0.
claims.scope: MovieLens-1M; K0/M1/M2 variants tested; multi-seed evidence for seeds 42/43/44.
limitations: M1 has doubled total supervision exposure relative to N-K0 in the fair-budget diagnostic.
M1 is not strictly better than N-K0 on ranking.
claims.allowed_language: M1 provides a unified multi-task compromise; N-K0 remains the cleaner ranking specialist.

claims.claim: LLM-vs-SASRec conclusions depend on the budget regime.
evidence: At roughly matched N-task sample exposure, N-K0 exceeds SASRec s23 by HR@1 0.2766519824 in seed 42.
The sample-efficiency curve shows N-K0 above closest-exposure SASRec points from roughly 3k to 24k N exposure.
At high exposure, SASRec s3000 exceeds N-K0 in all three seeds; minimum HR@1 margin 0.0777092511.
claims.scope: MovieLens-1M; PopMatch-k5; SASRec effective batch 512; LLM effective batch 8.
limitations: These are sample-exposure and step/exposure diagnostics, not strict FLOP-, wall-clock-, parameter-, or capacity-matched comparisons.
SASRec high-exposure rows must remain a separate regime.
claims.allowed_language: The LLM adapter is more sample efficient at low matched N-task exposure, whereas heavily trained SASRec is stronger in its high-exposure regime.

claims.claim: Canonical random-k5 ranking is too easy to interpret alone; PopMatch-k5 and candidate-size robustness are needed for credible ranking evidence.
evidence: Popularity and BPR-MF baselines are much stronger on canonical random-k5 than on PopMatch-k5.
N-K0 and M1 remain above popularity and BPR-MF under PopMatch-k5.
N-K0 remains above M1 under k20/k50 candidate-size stress tests.
claims.scope: MovieLens-1M; candidate protocols generated and evaluated in prior stages.
limitations: Candidate robustness is still offline evaluation, not an online recommendation setting.
Candidate protocol details must be printed with every table.
claims.allowed_language: Harder candidate controls reduce popularity shortcut concerns and preserve the main N-K0/M1 ranking pattern.
claims.forbidden_language: Canonical random-k5 alone proves recommender quality.
